verses.text: The family line began with Adam, Seth, and Enosh,
then Kenan, Mahalalel, and Jared,
then Enoch, Methuselah, and Lamech,
then Noah and his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was also Nimrod's father. Nimrod rose to become a mighty man on earth.
Mizraim was the ancestor of the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
as well as the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth. He was also the ancestor of
the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,
the Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,
and the Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.
Shem's descendants were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arpachshad was Shelah's father, and Shelah was Eber's father.
Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg because the earth was divided in his time. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, and Sheba,
and Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. These were all Joktan's sons.
The family line went from Shem to Arpachshad and Shelah,
then Eber, Peleg, and Reu,
then Serug, Nahor, and Terah,
then Abram, who was also called Abraham.
Abraham's sons were Isaac and Ishmael.
These were Ishmael's descendants: Nebaioth was his firstborn, followed by Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam,
then Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,
and Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were Ishmael's sons.
Abraham's concubine Keturah gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's sons were Sheba and Dedan.
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's descendants.
Abraham was Isaac's father. Isaac's sons were Esau and Israel.
Esau's sons were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
Eliphaz's descendants were Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
Reuel's sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
Seir's sons were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
Lotan's sons were Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan's sister.
Shobal's sons were Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah.
Anah's son was Dishon. Dishon's sons were Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
These were the kings who ruled Edom before Israel had a king. The first was Bela son of Beor, whose city was Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah took his place.
When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites took his place.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad took his place. Hadad defeated Midian in the fields of Moab, and his city was Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah took his place.
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth by the River took his place.
When Shaul died, Baal Hanan son of Achbor took his place.
When Baal Hanan died, Hadad took his place. His city was Pai. His wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab.
Then Hadad died. These were Edom's chiefs: Timna, Aliah, and Jetheth,
Oholibamah, Elah, and Pinon,
Kenaz, Teman, and Mibzar,
and Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.
Israel's sons were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun,
as well as Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
Judah's sons were Er, Onan, and Shelah, born to him by Shua's Canaanite daughter. Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the LORD's sight, and the LORD put him to death.
Judah's daughter-in-law Tamar gave birth to Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.
Perez's sons were Hezron and Hamul.
Zerah had five sons: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara.
Carmi's son was Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by taking what had been set apart for destruction.
Ethan's son was Azariah.
Hezron's sons were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, a leader of the people of Judah.
Nahshon was the father of Salma, and Salma was the father of Boaz.
Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse.
Jesse's firstborn son was Eliab, his second was Abinadab, and his third was Shimea.
His fourth son was Nethanel, and his fifth was Raddai.
His sixth was Ozem, and his seventh was David.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah had three sons: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail gave birth to Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron had children with his wife Azubah and with Jerioth. Her sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath. She bore him Hur.
Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.
Later, at sixty years old, Hezron married the daughter of Machir, who was Gilead's father. He slept with her, and she bore him Segub.
Segub was the father of Jair, who had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.
Geshur and Aram took Jair's towns from them, along with Kenath and its villages, sixty towns in all. These were all descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, had five sons: Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah, who was Onam's mother.
Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn, had three sons: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada. Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife was named Abihail. She bore him Ahban and Molid.
Nadab's sons were Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.
Appaim's son was Ishi, Ishi's son was Sheshan, and Sheshan's descendant was Ahlai.
Jada, Shammai's brother, had two sons, Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza. These were Jerahmeel's descendants.
Sheshan had daughters and no sons. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to his servant Jarha in marriage, and she bore him Attai.
Attai was the father of Nathan, and Nathan was the father of Zabad.
Zabad was the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jehu, and Jehu was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Helez, and Helez was the father of Eleasah.
Eleasah was the father of Sismai, and Sismai was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
Among the descendants of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were his firstborn Mesha, the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
Hebron's sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema was the father of Raham, who was the father of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
Caleb's concubine Ephah gave birth to Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was also the father of Gazez.
Jahdai's sons were Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb's concubine Maacah gave birth to Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Machbena and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, Ephrathah's firstborn: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim,
Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim, had these descendants: Haroeh and half the Menuhoth.
The families of Kiriath Jearim were the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. The Zorathites and Eshtaolites came from them.
Salma's descendants were Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, half the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
The families of scribes at Jabez were the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. They were the Kenites who descended from Hammath, the ancestor of Rechab's family.
These were David's sons born in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel. His second was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail from Carmel.
His third was Absalom, son of Maacah daughter of Talmai king of Geshur. His fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith.
His fifth was Shephatiah, son of Abital. His sixth was Ithream, son of his wife Eglah.
These six were born to David in Hebron, where he ruled for seven years and six months. He ruled for thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
In Jerusalem, Bathshua daughter of Ammiel bore him four sons: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
Nine other sons were born there: Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
These were David's sons, besides the sons of his concubines. Tamar was their sister.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam. The family line continued through Rehoboam's son Abijah, then Asa and Jehoshaphat,
then Joram, Ahaziah, and Joash,
then Amaziah, Azariah, and Jotham,
then Ahaz, Hezekiah, and Manasseh,
then Amon and Josiah.
Josiah's firstborn was Johanan, his second was Jehoiakim, his third was Zedekiah, and his fourth was Shallum.
Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
The sons of Jeconiah, who was taken captive, included Shealtiel,
as well as Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's sons included Meshullam and Hananiah, and Shelomith was their sister.
He also had five sons named Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab Hesed.
Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The family records also include the sons of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shecaniah.
Shecaniah's son was Shemaiah. The record counts six sons of Shemaiah and names Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
Neariah had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
Elioenai had seven sons: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
Judah's descendants included Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah son of Shobal was the father of Jahath, who was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the families of the Zorathites.
The sons of the father of Etam were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, Ephrathah's firstborn and the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives named Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were her sons.
Helah's sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz was the father of Anub and Zobebah and the ancestor of the families of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez because, she said, “I gave birth to him in sorrow.”
Jabez prayed to the God of Israel, “Please bless me and give me more land. May your hand be with me, and keep me from evil so I won't cause pain.” God gave him what he had asked for.
Chelub, Shuhah's brother, was the father of Mehir, and Mehir was the father of Eshton.
Eshton was the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of Ir Nahash. These were the people of Recah.
Kenaz's sons were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's son was Hathath.
Meonothai was the father of Ophrah, and Seraiah was the father of Joab. Joab was the father of Ge Harashim, whose people were craftsmen.
Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezrah's sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.

His wife from Judah bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. The family record also names the children of Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered married.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham, were the ancestors of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Ben Zoheth.
The descendants of Shelah son of Judah included Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the linen-working families from the house of Ashbea.
They also included Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash and Saraph, who held power in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These are old records.
These potters lived in Netaim and Gederah, where they worked for the king.
Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shaul's line continued through his son Shallum, then Mibsam and Mishma.
Mishma's line continued through his son Hammuel, then Zaccur and Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. His brothers had few children, and their whole family didn't grow as large as Judah's.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazarshual,
Bilhah, Ezem, and Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, and Ziklag,
and Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David became king.
They also had five villages: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
along with all the settlements around those towns as far as Baal. These were their homes, and they kept records of their family lines.
The leaders included Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, and Jehu son of Joshibiah, whose father was Seraiah son of Asiel.
They also included Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi, whose family line went back through Allon, Jedaiah, Shimri, and Shemaiah.
All those named were leaders of their families, and their households grew greatly.
They went as far as the entrance to Gedor and the east side of the valley to look for pasture for their flocks.
They found good, rich pasture in a wide, quiet, peaceful land. Descendants of Ham had lived there before them.

The men listed by name came during the reign of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the tents there and struck down the Meunim, destroying them completely. They settled there in their place because there was pasture for their flocks.
Five hundred men from Simeon's descendants went to Mount Seir. Their commanders were Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They struck down the Amalekites who had escaped, and they've lived there to this day.

This is the family of Reuben, Israel's firstborn. Reuben was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his birthright went to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. So the family record doesn't list him according to that birthright.
Judah became stronger than his brothers, and a ruler came from him, but the birthright belonged to Joseph.
Reuben, Israel's firstborn, had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Joel's family line continued through his son Shemaiah, then Gog and Shimei,
then Micah, Reaiah, and Baal,
and then Beerah. Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria took Beerah captive. He had been a leader of the Reubenites.
The records of his relatives by family listed Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,
and Bela son of Azaz, whose father was Shema son of Joel. Bela and his people lived at Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal Meon.
They settled eastward as far as the edge of the wilderness leading toward the Euphrates, because their herds had grown so large in Gilead.
In Saul's time they fought the Hagrites and defeated them. They moved into their tents throughout the land east of Gilead.
Gad's descendants lived next to them in Bashan, as far as Salecah.
Joel was their chief, Shapham was second, and Janai and Shaphat also lived in Bashan.
Their relatives, by household, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber, seven in all.
These were the descendants of Abihail son of Huri. His family line went back through Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel and grandson of Guni was the head of their families.
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon as far as their borders.
All these families were entered in the records in the days of King Jotham of Judah and King Jeroboam of Israel.

Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty men fit to go to war. They were brave fighters who could handle a shield and sword, shoot a bow, and fight skillfully.
They fought against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
They received help, and the Hagrites and their allies were handed over to them. They cried out to God in battle, and he answered because they trusted him.
They took fifty thousand camels, two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, and two thousand donkeys, and they took a hundred thousand people captive.
Many were killed because the battle was from God. The victors lived in their land until the exile.
The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land and grew numerous from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
Their family heads were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were brave warriors, well-known men who led their families.
But they were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors. They turned to the gods of the peoples God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up Pul king of Assyria and Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria. The Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were taken captive to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.
Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar was the father of Phinehas, and Phinehas was the father of Abishua.
Abishua was the father of Bukki, who was the father of Uzzi.
Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah, who was the father of Meraioth.
Meraioth was the father of Amariah, who was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok, who was the father of Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah, who was the father of Johanan.
Johanan was the father of Azariah, who served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah was the father of Amariah, who was the father of Ahitub.
Ahitub was the father of Zadok, who was the father of Shallum.
Shallum was the father of Hilkiah, who was the father of Azariah.
Azariah was the father of Seraiah, who was the father of Jehozadak.
Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem away through Nebuchadnezzar.
Levi's sons were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershom's sons were named Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans according to their family households.
Gershom's family line continued through his son Libni, then Jahath and Zimmah,
then Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai.
Kohath's family line continued through his son Amminadab, then Korah and Assir,
then Elkanah, Ebiasaph, and Assir,
then Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
Elkanah's sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.
Elkanah's line ran through his son Zophai, then Nahath,
then Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah.
Samuel's firstborn was Joel, and his second son was Abijah.
Merari's family line continued through Mahli and his son Libni, then Shimei and Uzzah,
then Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah.
These were the men David put in charge of music at the LORD's house after the ark had come to rest there.
They served as singers in front of the sanctuary, the Tent of Meeting, until Solomon built the LORD's house in Jerusalem. They carried out their duties in the appointed order.
These were the men who served, along with their sons. From the Kohathites came Heman the singer, son of Joel and grandson of Samuel.
His family line went back through Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel, and Toah,
then Zuph, Elkanah, Mahath, and Amasai,
then Elkanah, Joel, Azariah, and Zephaniah,
then Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph, and Korah,
then Izhar, Kohath, Levi, and Israel.
Heman's fellow Levite Asaph stood to his right. Asaph was the son of Berechiah and grandson of Shimea.
His family line went back through Michael, Baaseiah, and Malchijah,
then Ethni, Zerah, and Adaiah,
then Ethan, Zimmah, and Shimei,
then Jahath, Gershom, and Levi.
On the left stood their fellow Levites from Merari's family: Ethan son of Kishi, whose father was Abdi son of Malluch.
His family line went back through Hashabiah, Amaziah, and Hilkiah,
then Amzi, Bani, and Shemer,
then Mahli, Mushi, Merari, and Levi.
Their fellow Levites were appointed to all the other duties at the sanctuary of God's house.

Aaron and his sons made offerings on the altar of burnt offerings and on the altar of incense. They handled the work of the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel, following everything Moses, God's servant, had commanded.
This was Aaron's family line through his son Eleazar, then Phinehas and Abishua,
then Bukki, Uzzi, and Zerahiah,
then Meraioth, Amariah, and Ahitub,
then Zadok and Ahimaaz.
These were the places where the Levites settled within their territories. Aaron's descendants belonged to the Kohathite families and received the first allotment.
They were given Hebron in the land of Judah, along with its surrounding pasturelands.
The fields and villages belonging to Hebron went to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
Aaron's descendants received Hebron, a city of refuge, as well as Libnah with its pasturelands, Jattir, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands.
They also received Hilen and Debir, each with its pasturelands,
and Ashan and Beth Shemesh, each with its pasturelands.
From Benjamin they received Geba, Allemeth, and Anathoth, each with its pasturelands. Their families received thirteen towns in all.
The rest of Kohath's descendants were allotted ten towns from the families of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Gershom's descendants received thirteen towns for their families from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan.
Merari's descendants were allotted twelve towns for their families from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave the Levites towns and their pasturelands.
They allotted the towns named here from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Some families descended from Kohath received towns within the territory of Ephraim.
Among the towns given to them were Shechem, a city of refuge in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer, with their pasturelands.
They also received Jokmeam and Beth Horon with their pasturelands,
and Aijalon and Gath Rimmon with their pasturelands.
The other Kohathite families received Aner and Bileam from the half-tribe of Manasseh, with their pasturelands.
Gershom's descendants received Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth from the half-tribe of Manasseh, with their pasturelands.
From Issachar they received Kedesh and Daberath with their pasturelands,
and Ramoth and Anem with their pasturelands.
From Asher they received Mashal and Abdon with their pasturelands,
and Hukok and Rehob with their pasturelands.
From Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, each with its pasturelands.
The remaining Levites, Merari's descendants, received Rimmono and Tabor from Zebulun, with their pasturelands.
East of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they received Bezer in the wilderness and Jahzah from Reuben, with their pasturelands.
They also received Kedemoth and Mephaath with their pasturelands.
And from Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim with their pasturelands,
and Heshbon and Jazer with their pasturelands.
Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They led the families of Tola and were brave warriors in their generations. In David's time their fighting men numbered twenty-two thousand six hundred.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five were leaders.
The households of their descendants could field thirty-six thousand troops for battle, because they had many wives and sons.
The family records for all the clans of Issachar listed eighty-seven thousand brave warriors in all.
Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela's five sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were family heads and brave warriors. Their family records listed twenty-two thousand and thirty-four men.
Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. These were all his sons.
Their family records listed the heads of their households by generation, with twenty thousand two hundred brave warriors.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
These were the descendants of Jediael, listed by their family heads. They had seventeen thousand two hundred brave warriors fit to go out to battle.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir, and Hushim came from Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were descendants of Bilhah.
Manasseh's Aramean concubine bore him Asriel. She also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from the family of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister was named Maacah. The second was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, whose father was Manasseh.
Gilead's sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's family line included Shuthelah and his son Bered, then Tahath, Eleadah, and another Tahath.
It continued through Zabad and his son Shuthelah, and the family also included Ezer and Elead. The men native to Gath killed Ezer and Elead when they went down to take their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
He slept with his wife, and she became pregnant and bore a son. He named him Beriah because trouble had come on his family.
His daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower and Upper Beth Horon and Uzzen Sheerah.
His descendants included Rephah, then Resheph, Telah, and Tahan,
then Ladan, Ammihud, and Elishama,
then Nun and his son Joshua.
Their land and settlements included Bethel and its towns, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its towns to the west, and Shechem and its towns as far as Azzah and its towns.
Along the border of Manasseh they held Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor with their surrounding towns. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in those places.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were his children.
Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
His brother Helem's sons were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah,
as well as Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
These were Asher's descendants. They were heads of households, outstanding warriors, and leading officials. Their family records listed twenty-six thousand men fit for military service.
Benjamin was the father of Bela, his firstborn, Ashbel, his second, and Aharah, his third,
followed by Nohah, his fourth, and Rapha, his fifth.
Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, and Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, and Ahoah,
and Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These were Ehud's sons, the heads of the families who lived in Geba and were taken captive to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. Gera led them into exile and was the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim had children in the land of Moab after he sent away his wives Hushim and Baara.
His wife Hodesh bore him Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, and Malcam,
as well as Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirmah. These sons were heads of their families.
Hushim bore him Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons included Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod and its surrounding towns.
They also included Beriah and Shema, family heads among the people living in Aijalon. They drove the people of Gath away.
Beriah's sons included Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, and Eder,
and Michael, Ishpah, and Joha.
Elpaal's sons also included Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, and Heber,
along with Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab.
Shimei's sons included Jakim, Zichri, and Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel,
and Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath.
Shashak's sons included Ishpan, Eber, and Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, and Anthothijah,
and Iphdeiah and Penuel.
Jeroham's sons included Shamsherai, Shehariah, and Athaliah,
as well as Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri.
These were leading men, heads of their families as listed by generation. They lived in Jerusalem.
The father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
With them lived his firstborn son Abdon, along with Zur, Kish, Baal, and Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher,
and Mikloth, who was the father of Shimeah. They also lived with their families in Jerusalem, near their relatives.
Ner was the father of Kish, and Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea. Binea's family line continued through his son Raphah, then Eleasah and Azel.
Azel had six sons named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were all his sons.
His brother Eshek's firstborn was Ulam, his second was Jeush, and his third was Eliphelet.
Ulam's sons were brave warriors and skilled archers. They had many sons and grandsons, a hundred and fifty in all. These all belonged to Benjamin's family.
All Israel was listed by family in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Judah was taken captive to Babylon because of their disobedience.
The first to return and live on their own property in their towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
People from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.
Among them was Uthai son of Ammihud, from the line of Omri, Imri, and Bani, a descendant of Perez son of Judah.
From the Shilonites came Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.
From Zerah's descendants came Jeuel and his relatives, six hundred and ninety in all.
From Benjamin came Sallu son of Meshullam, whose family line went back through Hodaviah and Hassenuah.
There were also Ibneiah son of Jeroham, Elah son of Uzzi and grandson of Michri, and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, whose family line went back through Reuel and Ibnijah.
Their relatives numbered nine hundred and fifty-six according to the family records. The men listed were heads of their households.
The priests included Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
They also included Azariah son of Hilkiah, the officer in charge of God's house. His family line went back through Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub.
There were also Adaiah son of Jeroham, from the line of Pashhur and Malchijah, and Maasai son of Adiel, from the line of Jahzerah, Meshullam, Meshillemith, and Immer.
They and their relatives who led their households numbered one thousand seven hundred and sixty. They were skilled men able to do the work of serving in God's house.
The Levites included Shemaiah son of Hasshub, whose family line went back through Azrikam and Hashabiah to Merari.
They also included Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, from the line of Zichri and Asaph.
There were also Obadiah son of Shemaiah, from the line of Galal and Jeduthun, and Berechiah son of Asa and grandson of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their relatives. Shallum was their chief.
They had served at the King's Gate on the east side. They were the gatekeepers of the Levite camp.

Shallum was the son of Kore, whose family line went back through Ebiasaph to Korah. Shallum and his relatives, the Korahites, were responsible for guarding the entrances of the Tent. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to the LORD's camp.
Phinehas son of Eleazar had been in charge of them in earlier times, and the LORD was with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah guarded the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
There were two hundred and twelve men chosen to guard the entrances, listed by family in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted positions.
They and their descendants were responsible for guarding the gates of the LORD's house, the house of the Tent.
The gatekeepers stood on all four sides, to the east, west, north, and south.
Their relatives from the villages came to help them for seven days at a time.
The four chief gatekeepers were Levites in positions of trust. They were responsible for the rooms and the treasuries of God's house.
They spent the night around God's house because it was their job to guard it and open it every morning.
Some were responsible for the vessels used in worship. They counted them when they brought them in and when they took them out.
Others were responsible for the furnishings, all the vessels of the sanctuary, the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
Some of the priests' sons prepared the spice mixtures.
Mattithiah, a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with the things baked in pans.
Some of their relatives from Kohath's family were responsible for preparing the bread of the Presence every Sabbath.
The singers were heads of Levite households. They lived in the rooms and were excused from other duties because their work occupied them day and night.
These were leading men among the Levites, heads of their households according to their generations. They lived in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn was Abdon, followed by Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab,
then Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They also lived in Jerusalem alongside their relatives.
Ner was the father of Kish, and Kish was the father of Saul. Saul's sons were Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
Jonathan's son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
Micah's sons were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz was the father of Jarah. Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.
Moza was the father of Binea, whose line continued through Rephaiah, Eleasah, and Azel.
Azel had six sons named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel's sons.
The Philistines fought against Israel. Israel's men fled from them, and many fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons. They killed Saul's sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
The fighting grew fierce around Saul. The archers caught up with him, and he was in great distress.

Saul told his armor bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through before these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” His armor bearer was terrified and refused. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
When his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell on his own sword and died too.
So Saul and his three sons died, and his whole household fell with him.
When the Israelites in the valley saw their army running away and heard that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. The Philistines moved in and lived in them.
The next day the Philistines came to strip the dead. They found Saul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped Saul and took his head and armor. Then they sent messengers all through Philistine territory to announce the news to their idols and their people.
They put his armor in the temple of their gods and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon.
When everyone in Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
the brave men went and retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons. They brought them to Jabesh, buried their bones under the oak there, and fasted for seven days.
Saul died because he was unfaithful to the LORD. He didn't obey the LORD's word, and he went to a medium for advice
without asking the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and handed the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
All Israel came to David at Hebron and said, “We're your own flesh and bone.
Even when Saul was king, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing them back. The LORD your God told you, ‘You'll shepherd my people Israel and rule over them.’”
All Israel's elders came to the king at Hebron. David made a covenant with them there before the LORD, and they anointed him king over Israel, just as the LORD had said through Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, also called Jebus. The Jebusites who lived in the land were there.
The people of Jebus told David, “You won't get in here!” But David captured the fortress of Zion, which became David's City.
David had said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first will become commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and became commander.
David made his home in the fortress, so it was called David's City.
He built up the city all around, from the Millo outward, and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
David grew more and more powerful because the LORD of Armies was with him.
These were the leaders of David's mighty warriors. They backed him with all Israel to make him king and establish his rule, just as the LORD had said about Israel.
The list of David's mighty warriors begins with Jashobeam son of a Hachmonite, the leader of the Thirty. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them in one encounter.
Next was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the Three mighty warriors.
He was with David at Pasdammim when the Philistines gathered to fight. There was a field full of barley, and the people fled from the Philistines.
But David and his men stood in the middle of the field, defended it, and killed the Philistines. The LORD saved them with a great victory.
Three of the thirty leading warriors went down to David at the rock, at the cave of Adullam. The Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was in the stronghold, and the Philistines had a garrison at Bethlehem.
David said wistfully, “If only someone would get me a drink from the well by Bethlehem's gate!”
The three broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well by Bethlehem's gate, and brought it back to David. David refused to drink it. He poured it out to the LORD

and said, “God forbid I should drink it! Wouldn't it be like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives?” They'd put their lives on the line to bring it, so he wouldn't drink it. These were the things the three mighty warriors did.
Abishai, Joab's brother, led a group of three. He raised his spear against three hundred men and killed them. He earned a name among the three.
He was more honored than the other two and became their commander, though he wasn't counted as one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada, descended from a brave man of Kabzeel, did great deeds. He killed the two sons of Ariel from Moab. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
He killed an Egyptian who stood five cubits tall and carried a spear as thick as a weaver's beam. Benaiah went at him with a staff, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed him with it.
These were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He won a name among the three mighty warriors.
He was more honored than the Thirty, though he didn't rank among the Three. David put him in charge of his guard.
The army's mighty warriors included Asahel, Joab's brother, and Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite and Helez the Pelonite,
Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa and Abiezer from Anathoth,
Sibbecai the Hushathite and Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai from Netophah and Heled son of Baanah from Netophah,
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin and Benaiah from Pirathon,
Hurai from the streams of Gaash and Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite and Eliahba from Shaalbon,
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite and Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite and Eliphal son of Ur,
Hepher the Mecherathite and Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro from Carmel and Naarai son of Ezbai,
Joel, Nathan's brother, and Mibhar son of Hagri,
Zelek the Ammonite and Naharai the Berothite, who carried the armor of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite and Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite and Zabad son of Ahlai,
Adina son of Shiza, a Reubenite chief, with thirty men under him,
Hanan son of Maacah and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia from Ashterath, and Shama and Jeiel, the sons of Hotham from Aroer,
Jediael son of Shimri and his brother Joha the Tizite,
Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
and Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
These were the men who came to David at Ziklag while he was hiding from Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty warriors who helped him in battle.
They carried bows and could sling stones or shoot arrows with either hand. They were Saul's relatives from the tribe of Benjamin.
Their leader was Ahiezer, followed by Joash. Both were sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. There were also Jeziel and Pelet sons of Azmaveth, Beracah, and Jehu from Anathoth.
They included Ishmaiah from Gibeon, a mighty warrior and leader among the Thirty, along with Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederah,
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam from the Korahites,
and Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor.

Some men from Gad joined David at his stronghold in the wilderness. They were brave, trained fighters who could handle shield and spear. They had faces like lions and were as quick as gazelles in the mountains.
Ezer was their leader, Obadiah was second, and Eliab was third.
Mishmannah was fourth, and Jeremiah was fifth.
Attai was sixth, and Eliel was seventh.
Johanan was eighth, and Elzabad was ninth.
Jeremiah was tenth, and Machbannai was eleventh.
These men of Gad were army commanders. The least of them was a match for a hundred men, and the greatest for a thousand.
They crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it had flooded its banks, and drove away everyone who lived in the valleys on both sides.
Some people from Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.

David went out to meet them and said, “If you've come in peace to help me, I'll join with you wholeheartedly. If you've come to betray me to my enemies when I've done nothing wrong, may the God of our ancestors see it and rebuke you.”

Then the Spirit came on Amasai, the leader of the Thirty, and he said, “We're yours, David. We're on your side, son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, because your God helps you.” David welcomed them and made them commanders in his force.

Some men from Manasseh joined David when he went with the Philistines to fight Saul. David and his men didn't fight with them, because the Philistine rulers talked it over and sent him away. They said, “He may go back to his master Saul, and it will cost us our heads.”
As David went to Ziklag, men from Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, another Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai. They commanded units of a thousand in Manasseh.
They helped David against the raiding party. They were all brave warriors and became commanders in the army.
Day after day men came to help David until he had a great army, like the army of God.
These are the numbers of the troops equipped for battle who came to David at Hebron to hand Saul's kingdom over to him, just as the LORD had said.
From Judah came six thousand eight hundred men equipped for battle with shields and spears.
From Simeon came seven thousand one hundred brave warriors ready for battle.
From Levi came four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada led Aaron's family, and there were three thousand seven hundred with him.
Zadok was a brave young warrior, and twenty-two commanders came from his family.
From Benjamin, Saul's own tribe, came three thousand. Until then most of them had stayed loyal to Saul's family.
From Ephraim came twenty thousand eight hundred brave warriors, men well known in their families.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh came eighteen thousand men chosen by name to go and make David king.
From Issachar came two hundred leaders who understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do. All their relatives were under their command.
From Zebulun came fifty thousand men ready to take their places in battle with every kind of weapon. They stood together without divided loyalties.
From Naphtali came a thousand commanders and thirty-seven thousand men with shields and spears.
From Dan came twenty-eight thousand six hundred men ready to take their places in battle.
From Asher came forty thousand men fit for the army and ready for battle.
From the other side of the Jordan came a hundred and twenty thousand men from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. They were equipped with every kind of weapon for battle.
All these trained soldiers came to Hebron fully determined to make David king over all Israel. The rest of Israel was of one mind about making David king too.
They spent three days with David, eating and drinking. Their relatives had provided food for them.

People from nearby and from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought plenty of flour, fig cakes, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep, because there was joy in Israel.
David consulted all the leaders, including the commanders of thousands and hundreds.

Then David told the whole assembly of Israel, “If this seems right to you and it's what the LORD our God wants, let's send word throughout Israel. Let's call our fellow Israelites together, along with the priests and Levites who live among them in towns with pasturelands.
Let's bring God's ark back to us. We didn't seek it in Saul's time.”
The whole assembly agreed to do it, because it seemed right to everyone.
David gathered all Israel from the Shihor River of Egypt to the entrance of Hamath to bring God's ark back from Kiriath Jearim.
David and all Israel went to Baalah, also known as Kiriath Jearim, in Judah. They went to bring back the ark of the LORD God, who sits enthroned above the cherubim and whose name the ark bears.
They took God's ark from Abinadab's house on a new cart, with Uzza and Ahio driving it.
David and all Israel celebrated before God with all their strength, singing and playing harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they reached Chidon's threshing floor, the oxen stumbled, and Uzza reached out to steady the ark.
The LORD's anger burned against Uzza. He struck him for putting his hand on the ark, and Uzza died there before God.
David was upset because the LORD had broken out against Uzza. He named the place Perez Uzza, and it's still called that today.
David was afraid of God that day and asked, “How can I bring God's ark home with me?”
So David didn't take the ark with him into David's City. He took it instead to the house of Obed-Edom from Gath.
God's ark stayed with Obed-Edom's family in his house for three months. The LORD blessed Obed-Edom's household and everything he owned.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber, masons, and carpenters to build him a palace.
David realized that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had made his kingdom great for the sake of his people Israel.
David married more wives in Jerusalem and had more sons and daughters.
These were the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, and Elpelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went up to look for him. David heard about it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines had come and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” The LORD said, “Go. I'll hand them over to you.”

David and his men went up to Baal Perazim and defeated them there. David said, “God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like water breaking through a barrier.” So they named that place Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their gods behind. David ordered them burned.
The Philistines raided the valley again.
David asked God what to do again. God said, “Don't go straight up after them. Circle around and approach them from opposite the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the treetops, go out to fight. God will have gone ahead of you to strike the Philistine army.”
David did what God commanded, and his men struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon as far as Gezer.
David's fame spread to every land, and the LORD made all the nations fear him.
David built houses for himself in David's City. He prepared a place for God's ark and set up a tent for it.
Then David said, “Only the Levites should carry God's ark. The LORD chose them to carry it and serve him forever.”
David gathered all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the LORD's ark to the place he had prepared for it.
David assembled Aaron's descendants and the Levites:
from Kohath's descendants, Uriel their leader and a hundred and twenty of his relatives;
from Merari's descendants, Asaiah their leader and two hundred and twenty of his relatives;
from Gershom's descendants, Joel their leader and a hundred and thirty of his relatives;
from Elizaphan's descendants, Shemaiah their leader and two hundred of his relatives;
from Hebron's descendants, Eliel their leader and eighty of his relatives;
and from Uzziel's descendants, Amminadab their leader and a hundred and twelve of his relatives.
David summoned Zadok and Abiathar the priests and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

He told them, “You're the heads of the Levite families. Set yourselves and your relatives apart for this work, so you can bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I've prepared for it.
The LORD our God broke out against us in anger because you didn't carry it the first time. We hadn't asked him how to do it according to his instructions.”
So the priests and Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
The Levites carried God's ark on their shoulders with its poles, as Moses had commanded in keeping with the LORD's word.
David told the Levite leaders to appoint some of their relatives as singers and musicians. They were to play stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals and lift their voices loudly with joy.
The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel, his relative Asaph son of Berechiah, and Ethan son of Kushaiah from their relatives in Merari's family.

With them came their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-Edom and Jeiel.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were assigned to sound the bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played stringed instruments set to Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah led with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre.
Chenaniah, a Levite leader, was in charge of the singing. He taught the singers because he was skilled.
Berechiah and Elkanah guarded the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets ahead of God's ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah guarded the ark.
David, Israel's elders, and the commanders of thousands went joyfully to bring the ark of the LORD's covenant up from Obed-Edom's house.
Because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David wore a robe of fine linen, as did all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, who led the singers. David also wore a linen ephod.
All Israel brought up the ark of the LORD's covenant with shouts, horns, trumpets, cymbals, and the loud music of stringed instruments and harps.
As the ark of the LORD's covenant entered David's City, Saul's daughter Michal looked out the window. She saw King David dancing and celebrating and felt contempt for him.
They brought God's ark inside and set it in the middle of the tent David had pitched for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
When David had finished presenting the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the LORD's name.
He gave every Israelite, men and women alike, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
David appointed some of the Levites to serve before the LORD's ark, to remember his deeds and give thanks and praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was in charge, with Zechariah second. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel played stringed instruments and harps, and Asaph sounded the cymbals.
The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel regularly blew trumpets before the ark of God's covenant.
That day David first appointed Asaph and his relatives to give thanks to the LORD:
Give thanks to the LORD and call on his name. Tell the peoples what he's done.
Sing to him, sing his praises, and speak of all his wonderful works.
Take pride in his holy name. Let everyone who seeks the LORD rejoice from the heart.
Seek the LORD and his strength. Keep seeking his face always.
Remember the wonders he's done, his miracles and the judgments he's spoken,
you descendants of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen people.
He is the LORD our God. His judgments reach throughout the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the promise he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant he made with Abraham and the oath he swore to Isaac.
He confirmed it as a statute for Jacob, an everlasting covenant for Israel.
He said, “I'll give you the land of Canaan as your allotted inheritance,”
when you were very few and lived there as foreigners.
They traveled from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one harm them. He even rebuked kings for their sake:
“Don't touch my anointed ones, and do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Tell of his saving work day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations and his wonderful works among all peoples.
The LORD is great and deserves great praise. He is to be held in awe above all gods.
All the gods of the peoples are idols. The LORD made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and joy are where he dwells.
Give the LORD his due, families of the peoples. Give the LORD glory and strength!
Give the LORD the glory his name deserves. Bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in holy splendor.
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world stands firm and can't be moved.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice. Let people say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!”
Let the sea and everything in it roar. Let the fields and all they hold be glad.
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, because he's coming to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, because he is good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Say, “Save us, God our savior. Gather us and rescue us from the nations, so we can thank your holy name and rejoice in your praise.”
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! All the people said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD.
David left Asaph and his relatives there before the ark of the LORD's covenant to serve before it regularly, doing whatever each day required.
Obed-Edom and their sixty-eight relatives stayed as well. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests in front of the LORD's sanctuary at the high place in Gibeon.
They were to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offerings every morning and evening, in keeping with everything written in the LORD's law that he had given Israel.
Heman, Jeduthun, and the others chosen by name were with them to give thanks to the LORD, because his faithful love lasts forever.
Heman and Jeduthun were there with trumpets and cymbals to sound aloud and instruments for songs to God. Jeduthun's sons were assigned to the gate.
Then everyone went home, and David went back to bless his household.
Once David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house made of cedar, but the ark of the LORD’s covenant is in a tent.”
Nathan told David, “Go ahead with what’s on your heart. God is with you.”
That very night, God gave Nathan this message:
“Go tell my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD says: You won’t be the one to build me a house to live in.
I haven’t lived in a house from the day I brought Israel out until now. I’ve moved from one tent to the next.
Everywhere I went with Israel, I put judges in charge to shepherd my people. Did I ever ask any of them why they hadn’t built me a cedar house?’
“Now tell my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the sheep pen, where you followed the flock, and made you ruler over my people Israel.
I’ve been with you everywhere you’ve gone, and I’ve cut down your enemies before you. I’ll make your name as great as the names of the greatest people on earth.
I’ll choose a place for my people Israel and plant them there. They’ll live in a place of their own without being uprooted again. Wicked people won’t wear them down like they did at first,
back when I appointed judges over my people Israel. I’ll bring all your enemies under control. And I’m telling you this: the LORD will build a house for you.
When your days are over and you join your ancestors, I’ll raise up one of your own sons to succeed you, and I’ll establish his kingdom.
He’ll build a house for me, and I’ll establish his throne forever.
I’ll be his father, and he’ll be my son. I won’t withdraw my faithful love from him the way I withdrew it from the one who came before you.
I’ll give him a permanent place in my house and my kingdom. His throne will stand forever.’”
Nathan told David everything God had said and everything he had seen in the vision.
Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, LORD God, and who are my family, that you’ve brought me this far?
And as though that were a small thing to you, God, you’ve spoken about my family far into the future. LORD God, you’ve treated me like someone of high standing.
What else can I say about the honor you’ve given me? You already know your servant.
LORD, for my sake and in keeping with your own heart, you’ve done all these great things and made them known.
LORD, from everything we’ve heard with our own ears, there is no one like you and no God besides you.

What other nation on earth is like your people Israel? You went to rescue them and make them your own. You made a name for yourself through great and awesome acts, driving nations out ahead of the people you rescued from Egypt.
You made Israel your own people forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
Now, LORD, let the promise you made about me and my family stand forever. Do what you said.
May your name stand and be honored forever. May people say, ‘The LORD of Armies is Israel’s God. He is God to Israel, and the house of his servant David stands firm before him.’
My God, you revealed to me that you would build a house for me. That’s why I’ve found the courage to pray before you.
Now, LORD, you are God, and you’ve promised me this good thing.
You’ve chosen to bless my family so it can stand before you forever. LORD, you have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever.”
After this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Gath and its surrounding towns from them.
He also defeated Moab. The Moabites became his subjects and paid him tribute.
David defeated King Hadadezer of Zobah near Hamath when Hadadezer went to establish his rule by the Euphrates River.
David captured a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He cut the tendons of the chariot horses, sparing enough horses for a hundred chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came to help King Hadadezer of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand Syrians.
David stationed troops in the territory of Damascus, and the Syrians became his subjects and paid him tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem.
David took a large amount of bronze from Tibhath and Cun, two of Hadadezer's cities. Solomon used it to make the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
When King Tou of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of King Hadadezer of Zobah,
he sent his son Hadoram to greet King David and congratulate him on defeating Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of gold, silver, and bronze vessels.
King David dedicated these to the LORD along with the silver and gold he had taken from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek.
Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He stationed troops in Edom, and all the Edomites became David's subjects. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
David ruled over all Israel and made sure all his people were treated justly and fairly.
Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar served as priests, and Shavsha was the scribe.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons were senior officials in the king's service.
Afterward Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son took his place.
David said, "I'll show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash because his father showed kindness to me." So he sent messengers into Ammonite territory to offer Hanun condolences for his father's death.
But the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, "Do you think David sent these men because he wants to honor your father? Haven't they come to scout the land, spy on it, and overthrow it?"
So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, cut their clothes off at the buttocks, and sent them away.
When David heard how the men had been treated, he sent people to meet them because they had been deeply humiliated. The king told them, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then come home."
When the Ammonites realized how badly they had offended David, Hanun and his people sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his people, who came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites gathered from their towns and came out for battle.
When David heard, he sent Joab with the whole army of his best fighters.
The Ammonites lined up for battle at the city gate, while the kings who had come stayed apart in the open field.
Joab saw that he was facing battle on two fronts, so he picked some of Israel's best men and lined them up against the Syrians.
He put his brother Abishai in charge of the rest of the troops, who lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, come help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come help you.
Be brave. Let's stand strong for our people and the cities of our God. May the LORD do what seems good to him."
Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from him.
When the Ammonites saw the Syrians flee, they ran from Joab's brother Abishai and retreated into the city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they sent messengers to bring in Syrians from beyond the Euphrates. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David heard, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and took up positions against them. The Syrians met him in battle.
The Syrians ran from Israel. David killed seven thousand Syrian chariot drivers and forty thousand foot soldiers, as well as Shophach, their commander.
When Hadadezer's subjects saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his subjects. The Syrians gave the Ammonites no more help.

At the turn of the year, when kings usually go out to war, Joab led out the army, devastated the Ammonite countryside, and laid siege to Rabbah. David stayed in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and captured it.
David took the crown off their king's head. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones. The crown was placed on David's head, and he carried a great deal of plunder out of the city.
David brought the people out of the city and had them cut with saws, iron picks, and axes. He did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his people returned to Jerusalem.
Later, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, one of the giant's descendants, and the Philistines were subdued.
When war broke out with the Philistines again, Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath from Gath. The shaft of Lahmi's spear was as thick as a weaver's beam.
In another battle at Gath there was a huge man with twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot. He too was descended from the giant.
When he defied Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, killed him.
These men were descendants of the giant in Gath. They fell at the hands of David and his men.
Satan rose up against Israel and stirred David to take a census of the people.
David told Joab and the leaders of the people, "Go count the people of Israel from Beersheba to Dan. Report back so I can know how many there are."
Joab said, "May the LORD make his people a hundred times as numerous as they are now. But my lord the king, aren't they all your servants? Why do you want this done? Why bring guilt on Israel?"
The king overruled Joab. So Joab went through all Israel and then returned to Jerusalem.
Joab reported the census totals to David. In Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men able to carry a sword, and in Judah there were four hundred seventy thousand.
Joab left Levi and Benjamin out of the count because he found the king's order repulsive.
God was displeased by what David had done, so he struck Israel.
David said to God, "I've sinned terribly by doing this. Please take away your servant's guilt. I've acted very foolishly."
The LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer.
"Go tell David, 'The LORD says: I'm giving you three choices. Pick one, and I'll do it to you.'"
Gad went to David and said, "The LORD says, 'Choose:

three years of famine, three months of being overwhelmed by your foes while their swords overtake you, or three days of the LORD's sword, with plague in the land and the LORD's angel bringing destruction throughout Israel.' Think it over and tell me what answer to take back to the one who sent me."
David told Gad, "I'm in terrible distress. Please let me fall into the LORD's hands, because his mercy is great. Keep me from falling into human hands."
So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel died.

God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. Just as the angel was about to destroy it, the LORD saw what was happening and relented. He told the angel bringing destruction, "Enough. Pull back your hand." The LORD's angel was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David looked up and saw the LORD's angel standing between earth and sky, with a drawn sword stretched out over Jerusalem. David and the elders put their faces to the ground in sackcloth.

David said to God, "I'm the one who ordered the census. I sinned and did something terribly wrong. But what have these sheep done? LORD my God, please let your hand fall on me and my father's family, and spare your people from the plague."
The LORD's angel told Gad to tell David to go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
David went up as Gad had told him to do in the LORD's name.
Ornan was threshing wheat when he turned and saw the angel. His four sons, who were there with him, hid.
As David approached, Ornan saw him, came out from the threshing floor, and bowed before David with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, "Sell me this threshing floor so I can build an altar to the LORD here. Sell it to me at full price, so the plague on the people can be stopped."

Ornan told David, "Take it. My lord the king can do whatever seems right to him. I'll give you the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing tools for firewood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give you all of it."
King David answered Ornan, "No. I'll buy it at full price. I won't take what belongs to you and give it to the LORD, or make a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.
David built an altar to the LORD there and presented burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, who answered him with fire from heaven on the altar for burnt offerings.
The LORD gave the angel an order, and the angel put his sword back in its sheath.
When David saw that the LORD had answered him at Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor, he offered sacrifices there.
At that time the LORD's tabernacle, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar for burnt offerings were at the high place in Gibeon.
David was too afraid of the LORD's angel and his sword to go there to ask God for guidance.
Then David said, "This is the site of the house of the LORD God, and this is where Israel's altar for burnt offerings belongs."
David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to be gathered, and he assigned stonecutters to shape blocks for God's house.
He stockpiled iron for the nails in the gate doors and for the fittings, and more bronze than anyone could weigh.
He also gathered more cedar logs than anyone could count, because the people of Sidon and Tyre brought him so many.

David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house for the LORD must be magnificent, famous and honored in every land. I'll get things ready for it." So David made extensive preparations before he died.
Then he called for his son Solomon and charged him with building a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
David told Solomon, "I wanted to build a house that would honor the name of the LORD my God.
But the LORD gave me this message: 'You've shed a great deal of blood and fought major wars. You won't build a house to honor my name, because you've shed so much blood on the earth in my sight.
You will have a son who will be a man of peace. I'll give him rest from the enemies all around him. His name will be Solomon, and I'll give Israel peace and quiet while he lives.
He will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I'll establish his royal throne over Israel forever.'
Now, my son, may the LORD be with you and give you success as you build the house of the LORD your God, just as he said you would.
May the LORD give you good judgment and understanding when he puts you in charge of Israel, so you can keep the law of the LORD your God.
You'll succeed if you carefully follow the statutes and rulings the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave. Don't be afraid or lose heart.

Look, even in my hardship I've set aside a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and more bronze and iron than anyone can weigh, all for the LORD's house. I've also gathered timber and stone, and you can add more.
You have plenty of workers, including stonecutters, stoneworkers, carpenters, and people skilled in every kind of work.
There's more gold, silver, bronze, and iron than anyone can count. Get up and get to work, and may the LORD be with you."
David also told all Israel's leaders to help his son Solomon. He said,
"Isn't the LORD your God with you? Hasn't he given you peace on every side? He handed the people of this land over to me, and the land is now under the authority of the LORD and his people.

So give your whole heart and soul to following the LORD your God. Get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so you can bring the ark of the LORD's covenant and God's sacred vessels into the house built for the LORD's name."
When David was old and had lived a long life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He brought together all Israel's leaders, along with the priests and Levites.
The Levite men who were thirty years old and up were counted one by one. There were thirty-eight thousand of them.
David said, "Twenty-four thousand of these men will oversee the work at the LORD's house, and six thousand will serve as officers and judges.
Four thousand will guard the doors, and four thousand will praise the LORD with the instruments I made for that purpose."
David organized them into groups by their descent from Levi's sons Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The Gershonite lines were Ladan and Shimei.
Ladan had three sons: Jehiel, who was the head, Zetham, and Joel.
Shimei had three sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. These were the heads of Ladan's families.
Shimei had four sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.
Jahath was the head, and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah had few sons, so their families were counted together as one household.
Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his sons were set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, burn incense before the LORD, serve him, and pronounce blessings in his name.
The sons of Moses, the man of God, were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
Shebuel was the head of Gershom's family.
Eliezer's son Rehabiah was the head. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had many sons.
Shelomith was the head of Izhar's family.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah, who was the head, then Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
Uzziel's sons were Micah, who was the head, and Isshiah, who was second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died leaving daughters and no sons. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them.
Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
These were Levi's descendants by family, including the heads of the families. The men twenty years old and up who worked in the service of the LORD's house were listed and counted by name.
David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people rest, and he lives in Jerusalem forever.
So the Levites no longer have to carry the tabernacle or any of the equipment used in its service."
Under David's final instructions, Levi's descendants were counted from twenty years old and up.
Their job was to help Aaron's descendants serve at the LORD's house. They looked after the courtyards and rooms, purified all the sacred things, and did the work needed at God's house.
They also looked after the bread set before God, the fine flour for grain offerings, the unleavened wafers, the offerings baked in pans or prepared by soaking, and every measure of quantity and size.
Each morning and evening they were to stand and thank and praise the LORD.
They were also to present the burnt offerings to the LORD on Sabbaths, at new moons, and at the appointed festivals, regularly offering the prescribed number before him.
They were to carry out their duties for the Tent of Meeting and the holy place and help their fellow Levites, Aaron's descendants, in serving at the LORD's house.
Aaron's descendants were organized into divisions. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no children, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, with Zadok from Eleazar's line and Ahimelech from Ithamar's line, divided them into groups according to the order in which they would serve.
Eleazar's line had more family heads than Ithamar's line. There were sixteen family heads from Eleazar and eight from Ithamar, and the groups were divided accordingly.
They assigned the groups impartially by drawing lots. Both Eleazar's and Ithamar's families had officials who served in God's sanctuary and officials who served God.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite scribe, recorded their names before the king, the leaders, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of priestly and Levite families. One family was drawn for Eleazar and one for Ithamar.
The first lot went to Jehoiarib and the second to Jedaiah.
The third went to Harim and the fourth to Seorim.
The fifth went to Malchijah and the sixth to Mijamin.
The seventh went to Hakkoz and the eighth to Abijah.
The ninth went to Jeshua and the tenth to Shecaniah.
The eleventh went to Eliashib and the twelfth to Jakim.
The thirteenth went to Huppah and the fourteenth to Jeshebeab.
The fifteenth went to Bilgah and the sixteenth to Immer.
The seventeenth went to Hezir and the eighteenth to Happizzez.
The nineteenth went to Pethahiah and the twentieth to Jehezkel.
The twenty-first went to Jachin and the twenty-second to Gamul.
The twenty-third went to Delaiah and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
This set the order in which they entered the LORD's house to serve, following the instructions handed down by their ancestor Aaron as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Among the other descendants of Levi, Amram's line included Shubael, and Shubael's line included Jehdeiah.
Isshiah was the head of Rehabiah's family.
Shelomoth was from Izhar's line, and Jahath was from Shelomoth's line.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, and Jekameam fourth.
Uzziel's line included Micah, and Micah's line included Shamir.
Micah's brother was Isshiah, and Isshiah's line included Zechariah.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Jaaziah's son was Beno.
Merari's descendants through Jaaziah were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Mahli's line included Eleazar, who had no sons.
Kish's son was Jerahmeel.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the Levites listed by family.

Like their relatives descended from Aaron, they too drew lots before King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families. The oldest brother's family and the youngest brother's family drew lots on equal terms.

David and the army commanders set apart some of the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to prophesy with harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals. The musicians were organized for service as follows.
Asaph's sons were Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. They served under their father Asaph, who prophesied at the king's direction.
Jeduthun had six sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah. They served under their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the harp as he gave thanks and praised the LORD.
