Heman's sons were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer, who spoke God's words. God raised Heman's standing and gave him fourteen sons and three daughters.
They all sang in the LORD's house under their fathers' direction, using cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps to serve in God's house. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman served under the king's direction.
Counting them and their relatives, there were two hundred eighty-eight skilled singers trained to sing to the LORD.
They drew lots for their assignments on equal terms, regardless of rank or whether they were teachers or students.
The first lot went to Joseph from Asaph's family. The second went to Gedaliah, whose group totaled twelve with his sons and brothers.
The third went to Zaccur and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The fourth went to Izri and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The fifth went to Nethaniah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The sixth went to Bukkiah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The seventh went to Jesharelah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The eighth went to Jeshaiah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The ninth went to Mattaniah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The tenth went to Shimei and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The eleventh went to Azarel and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twelfth went to Hashabiah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The thirteenth went to Shubael and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The fourteenth went to Mattithiah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The fifteenth went to Jeremoth and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The sixteenth went to Hananiah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The seventeenth went to Joshbekashah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The eighteenth went to Hanani and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The nineteenth went to Mallothi and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twentieth went to Eliathah and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twenty-first went to Hothir and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twenty-second went to Giddalti and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twenty-third went to Mahazioth and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
The twenty-fourth went to Romamti-Ezer and his sons and brothers, twelve in all.
Here are the gatekeeper divisions. From the Korahites came Meshelemiah son of Kore, a descendant of Asaph.
Meshelemiah's sons were Zechariah, his firstborn, then Jediael, Zebadiah, and Jathniel.
Elam was fifth, Jehohanan sixth, and Eliehoenai seventh.
Obed-Edom's first five sons were Shemaiah, his firstborn, then Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, and Nethanel.
Ammiel was sixth, Issachar seventh, and Peullethai eighth. God had blessed Obed-Edom.
Obed-Edom's son Shemaiah had sons who became leaders in their family because they were capable and courageous men.
Shemaiah's sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. Their relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also courageous men.
All these were Obed-Edom's descendants, together with their sons and brothers. There were sixty-two men from Obed-Edom's family, all strong and capable of doing the work.
Meshelemiah's sons and brothers numbered eighteen courageous men.
Hosah, a descendant of Merari, also had sons. Shimri was the head. His father had appointed him head even though he was younger than the firstborn.
Hilkiah was second, Tebaliah third, and Zechariah fourth. Hosah's sons and brothers numbered thirteen in all.
These leaders headed the gatekeeper divisions and had duties alongside their relatives in the service of the LORD's house.
They drew lots by family for each gate, with families of every rank taking part.
The east gate fell by lot to Shelemiah. Then they drew lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and he was assigned the north gate.
Obed-Edom was assigned the south gate, and his sons were assigned the storehouse.
Shuppim and Hosah were assigned the west side, by the Shallecheth Gate on the uphill road, with guards stationed across from each other.
Six Levites were posted on the east, four each day on the north, four each day on the south, and two at each storehouse post.
On the west, four were posted on the road and two at Parbar.
These were the gatekeeper divisions from the families of Korah and Merari.
Among the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of God's house and the treasuries holding dedicated gifts.
Jehieli was among the family heads descended from Ladan of the Gershonites.
Jehieli's sons Zetham and his brother Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the LORD's house.
There were also duties among the families of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the overseer of the treasuries.
His relatives in Eliezer's line were Eliezer's son Rehabiah and his descendants in order: Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries holding gifts dedicated by King David, the family heads, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.
They had dedicated some of the plunder from battles to repair the LORD's house.
Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, Joab son of Zeruiah, or anyone else was in the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.
From Izhar's family, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed as officers and judges, handling Israel's affairs outside the sanctuary.
From Hebron's family, Hashabiah and his brothers, seventeen hundred capable men, oversaw Israel west of the Jordan in matters concerning the LORD and the king's service.
Jerijah was the head of the Hebronites according to their family records. In the fortieth year of David's reign a search through their families found men of courage at Jazer in Gilead.

Jerijah had twenty-seven hundred capable relatives who were family heads. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh in all matters concerning God and the king.

Here is the count of the Israelites who served the king: family heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and their officers. Their divisions rotated in and out of service each month throughout the year, with twenty-four thousand in each division.
Jashobeam son of Zabdiel led the first division, which served in the first month and numbered twenty-four thousand.
He descended from Perez and was in charge of all the army commanders for the first month.
Dodai the Ahohite led the division for the second month, with Mikloth as its officer. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada the chief priest was the third army commander, serving in the third month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
This was the Benaiah who was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and led them. His son Ammizabad served with his division.
Asahel, Joab's brother, commanded the fourth division in the fourth month, and his son Zebadiah succeeded him. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Shamhuth the Izrahite commanded the fifth division in the fifth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite commanded the sixth division in the sixth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Helez the Pelonite, from Ephraim, commanded the seventh division in the seventh month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Sibbecai the Hushathite, from the Zerahites, commanded the eighth division in the eighth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Abiezer the Anathothite, from Benjamin, commanded the ninth division in the ninth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Maharai the Netophathite, from the Zerahites, commanded the tenth division in the tenth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Benaiah the Pirathonite, from Ephraim, commanded the eleventh division in the eleventh month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
Heldai the Netophathite, from Othniel's family, commanded the twelfth division in the twelfth month. His division numbered twenty-four thousand.
These were the leaders of Israel's tribes: Eliezer son of Zichri led Reuben, and Shephatiah son of Maacah led Simeon.
Hashabiah son of Kemuel led Levi, and Zadok led Aaron's family.
Elihu, one of David's brothers, led Judah, and Omri son of Michael led Issachar.
Ishmaiah son of Obadiah led Zebulun, and Jeremoth son of Azriel led Naphtali.
Hoshea son of Azaziah led Ephraim, and Joel son of Pedaiah led half the tribe of Manasseh.
Iddo son of Zechariah led the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, and Jaasiel son of Abner led Benjamin.
Azarel son of Jeroham led Dan. These were the leaders of Israel's tribes.
David left those twenty years old and younger out of the count, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Joab son of Zeruiah started counting the people but never finished. Wrath came on Israel because of this, and the count was left out of King David's official records.
Azmaveth son of Adiel managed the king's treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah managed the stores in the countryside, cities, villages, and towers.
Ezri son of Chelub supervised the workers who cultivated the fields.
Shimei the Ramathite oversaw the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite managed the wine going into the cellars.
Baal Hanan the Gederite oversaw the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands, and Joash managed the oil stores.
Shitrai the Sharonite oversaw the herds grazing in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai oversaw the herds in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite managed the camels. Jehdeiah the Meronothite managed the donkeys. Jaziz the Hagrite managed the flocks.
These were the people in charge of King David's property.
David's uncle Jonathan was an adviser, a man of good judgment, and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king's adviser, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar came after Ahithophel. Joab commanded the king's army.

David gathered all Israel's leaders in Jerusalem: the tribal leaders, the officers of the divisions that served the king in turn, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the supervisors of the king's property and his sons' possessions, the officials, and all the bravest warriors.

King David stood and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I wanted to build a house where the ark of the LORD's covenant, the footstool of our God, could rest. I made preparations to build it.
But God told me, 'You won't build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

Still, the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of my father's whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to lead, my father's household out of the tribe of Judah, and me out of my father's sons. It pleased him to make me king over all Israel.
The LORD gave me many sons, and from among them he chose Solomon to sit on the throne of the LORD's kingdom over Israel.
He told me, 'Your son Solomon will build my house and its courts. I've chosen him as my son, and I'll be his father.
I'll establish his kingdom forever if he keeps following my commands and rulings as he does today.'

So here, in front of all Israel, the LORD's assembly, and within the hearing of our God, study and keep every command of the LORD your God. Then you can hold on to this good land and leave it to your children as an inheritance forever.

As for you, my son Solomon, know your father's God and serve him wholeheartedly, with a willing mind. The LORD searches every heart and understands the motives behind every thought. If you seek him, you'll find him. If you abandon him, he'll reject you forever.
Pay attention, because the LORD has chosen you to build a house for his sanctuary. Be strong and get it done."
Then David gave Solomon the plans for the temple porch, its buildings, treasuries, upper rooms, inner rooms, and the place for the mercy seat.
He also gave him the plans he had received through the Spirit for the courts of the LORD's house, all the surrounding rooms, the treasuries of God's house, and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts.
He gave him instructions for the divisions of priests and Levites, for all the work of serving at the LORD's house, and for all the vessels used there.
He specified the weight of gold for every kind of gold vessel and the weight of silver for every kind of silver vessel used in the work.
He gave the weight of gold for each gold lampstand and its lamps, and the weight of silver for each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to how each lampstand would be used.
He specified the weight of gold for each table that held the bread set before God, and the silver for the silver tables.
He gave instructions for the pure gold forks, basins, and cups, and the weight of gold or silver for each bowl.
He specified the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense and gave the design for the gold chariot, the cherubim whose wings spread out over the ark of the LORD's covenant.
David said, "The LORD's hand showed me all this in writing, every detail of the work in these plans."

David told his son Solomon, "Be strong and brave, and do the work. Don't be afraid or lose heart, because the LORD God, my God, is with you. He'll stay with you and see you through until all the work for the LORD's house is finished.

The divisions of the priests and Levites are ready for all the service at God's house. Skilled workers who are willing to serve will help you with every kind of work. The leaders and all the people will follow your orders."
King David told the whole assembly, "God has chosen my son Solomon alone. He's still young and inexperienced, and this is a huge undertaking. This palace is for the LORD God himself.

I've done everything I can to prepare for my God's house: gold for gold items, silver for silver items, bronze for bronze items, iron for iron items, and wood for wooden items. I've also gathered onyx, stones for settings, different colors of stone for inlay, all kinds of precious stones, and plenty of marble.
Because my heart is set on my God's house, I'm giving my own gold and silver to it on top of everything I've already prepared for the holy house.
I'm giving three thousand talents of gold from Ophir and seven thousand talents of refined silver to cover the walls of the buildings,
to supply gold and silver for their respective items and for all the work the craftspeople will do. Who is willing to dedicate themselves to the LORD today?"
The family heads, the leaders of Israel's tribes, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the supervisors of the king's work all gave willingly.

For the work on God's house they gave five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
Those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the LORD's house, which Jehiel the Gershonite managed.
The people celebrated because they had given freely and wholeheartedly to the LORD. King David was overjoyed as well.
David praised the LORD in front of the whole assembly and said, "You are blessed forever and ever, LORD, God of our father Israel.
LORD, greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty are yours. Everything in heaven and on earth belongs to you. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are lifted up as ruler over all.
Wealth and honor come from you, and you rule over everything. Power and might are in your hands. You have the power to make anyone great and give them strength.
So now, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we can give so freely? Everything comes from you. We've given back what already belongs to you.
Before you we're strangers and foreigners, just as our ancestors were. Our days on earth pass like a shadow and leave nothing behind.
LORD our God, everything we've gathered to build a house for your holy name comes from your hand. It all belongs to you.
My God, I know you test the heart and take pleasure in honesty. I've given all these things freely and sincerely. And now I've had the joy of seeing your people here give willingly to you.
LORD, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire alive in your people's hearts forever and turn their hearts toward you.
Give my son Solomon a wholehearted commitment to keep your commands, testimonies, and statutes, to do everything required, and to build the palace I've made provision for."
Then David told the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God!" They all praised the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and bowed with their faces to the ground before the LORD and the king.
The next day they brought sacrifices and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, their drink offerings, and many sacrifices for all Israel.
They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. They made Solomon son of David king a second time and anointed him before the LORD as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
Solomon took his father David's place as king on the LORD's throne. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the leaders and warriors, including all of King David's sons, submitted to King Solomon.
The LORD made Solomon very great in the eyes of all Israel and gave him royal splendor beyond that of any king before him in Israel.
David son of Jesse had ruled over all Israel.
He ruled Israel for forty years, seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age after a long life of wealth and honor. His son Solomon succeeded him as king.
King David's deeds, from beginning to end, are recorded in the histories of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer,
along with his entire reign, his mighty deeds, and what happened to him, to Israel, and to all the kingdoms of the surrounding lands.
